newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
KATHIMERINI

--The government's new economic measures, while targeted at all incomes, will hit middle income earners hardest. The tough 1997 budget is being put together day by day amidst objections from within the ruling party PASOK.
--Brussels issues a warning to Greece to rein in its deficits quickly or risk losing Cohesion Fund monies.
--Turkish fighter planes violate Greek air space yesterday on the final day of the Greek Parmenion military exercise in the Aegean.
--Municipalities have begun voicing their complaints about the government's planned drastic cut backs in public expenditures. Sources say a strike is in the pipeline.
--The violent response to the Greenpeace blockade of the Motor Oil refinery is beamed around the world. Merchant Marine Minister Stavros Soumakis says the operation was "overzealous".
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Some 400 of the 800 tax breaks on the books are to go, following the approval of Prime Minister Costas Simitis at the meeting with economic ministers yesterday.
--As the world bows to US President Bill Clinton, Athens awaits word of his promised initiatives on the Aegean and Cyprus.
Clinton aide George Stephanopoulos says the new plan will have been developed in the first three months of the new year.
--University students block a downtown road to protest lack of teaching staff and other education issues.
TA NEA

--The Supreme Court's prosecutor orders a preliminary investigation into irregularities in state bodies and utilities regarding public funds and placing of contracts. The investigation will be carried out across the country.
--The government hopes to bring in 300 billion drachmas with its two bills on tax exemptions and spending cutbacks.
ETHNOS

--The 4,865 families earning more than 20 million drachmas per annum will be forced to pay for all their medical expenses. The less affluent, however, will lose their tax breaks on tutorial and lawyers' fees and donations.
--Six Greek-Americans in the US Congress will be ready to support Greece's national interests.
--Navy robot locates the sunken gunboat 'Kostakos' at a depth of 145 metres, off the Aegean island of Samos.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--The main opposition New Democracy party will hold a 'peace meeting' today after late-night consultations to try to find a way to avert the possibility of a split in the conservative party.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
